FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard [P : 14] (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
finalized by the Methods of Sampling and Test for Petroleum, its Products, Gaseous Fuels and Lubricants Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Product Division Council. 


This standard was originally published in 1960 which was an adaptation of ASTM D 156. This revision is taken 
up to update the standard in line with ASTM D 156 : 2015 ‘Standard Test Method for Saybolt Color of Petroleum 
Products (Saybolt Chromometer Method). 


In this revision, the requirements for petroleum hydrocarbon solvents was also included since color is a critical 
test for these products. Color of the product is an important characteristic since it can be readily observed by 
the user and may form the basis for either acceptance or rejection, even without any further testing. Although, 
measurement of the color of petroleum products is primarily aimed at manufacturing control and serves as an 
indication of the degree of refining and uniformity of the refining process. For any product having known color 
range, a deviation outside this range can indicate possible contamination with another product having a distinctly 
different color range. However, color may not always be a reliable indicator of product quality and hence should 
not be indiscreetly used in isolation in framing product specifications 


In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or 
calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 *Rules for rounding off numerical 
values (revised V. 


IS 1448 [P : 14] : 2019 


Indian Standard 


METHODS OF TEST FOR PETROLEUM 
AND ITS PRODUCTS 


[P:14] 
COLOUR BY SAYBOLTCHROMOMETER 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This Indian Standard [P : 14] describe the method 
intended for the determination of color of refined 
oils such as undyed motor and aviation gasoline’s, jet 
propulsion fuels, naphthas, petroleum hydrocarbon 
solvents and kerosene, and, in addition, petroleum 
waxes and pharmaceutical white oils. 


2 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this method, the following definition 
shall apply. 


2.1 Saybolt Colour — A number related to the depth 
of a column of material, the color of which is compared 
with specified glass standards. The range of numbers is 
+30 (lightest color) to -16 (darkest color). 


3 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


The height of a column of sample is decreased by 
levels corresponding to color numbers until the color 
of the material is unmistakably lighter than that of 
the standard. The color number above this level is 
reported regardless of whether the material was darker, 
questionable, or a match at the higher level. 


4 APPARATUS 


4.1 The Saybolt Chromometer 


Illustrated in Fig.l consists of sample and standard 
tubes, optical system, light source, and colour standards. 
The different parts of the chromometer are described 
in 4.1.1 to 4.1.10. 


4.1.1 Oil Sample Tube 


For testing liquids, use a No. 7740 Pyrex glass tube, or 
its equivalent in color characteristics (see Note), having 
an inside diameter of not less than 16:5 mm nor more 
than 17:5 mm, and an outside diameter of not less than 
21.25 mm nor more than 22:75 mm. Close the tube 
at the bottom with an optically clear plano glass disc 
6:25 mm thick, free of striations and scratches. The 
tube shall be 508 to 510 mm long from the upper 
surface of the plano disc to the top of the tube. Mount 
the tube and disc in a suitable metal collar provided 
with a petcock to permit controlled drainage of the tube 
(see Fig. 1). Construct the collar in a manner that 


permits removal of the glass disc for cleaning. Etch at 
intervals of every 25:4 mm a line completely around the 
tube starting at a point which will be 50:8 mm above the 
topsurface ofthe plano disc when the tube is in the collar. 
Number these lines consecutively 2 to 20 starting with 
the lowest ring. Graduate each 25.4 mm interval into 
8 equal sub-divisions. 
NOTE — The condition and the color of the glass tubes shall 
be such that no color difference is observed between the plain 
tube and the oil tube when the tubes are empty, or when the 
oil tube is filled with distilled water. Comparisons shall be 
made with the tubes positioned in the instrument in the manner 
described in 5. 


4.1.2 Wax Sample Tube 


For testing petroleum waxes, use an oil tube that 
meets the requirements given in 4.1.1 and that has a 
60-W heater evenly distributed over its entire length, 
as shown in Fig. 2. Alternative means may be used for 
keeping the wax in a liquid state and providing a means 
of readability of the graduated scale. 


4.1.3 Plain Tube 


Use a No. 7740 Pyrex glass tube or its equivalent in 
color characteristics (see Note), 483 mm long, meeting 
the diameter. Specifications given in 4.1.1 and open 
at both ends, with one end mounted in a suitable 
metal collar. The overall length of the tube and collar, 
assembled, shall be 516 to 518 mm. The collar provides 
a place to locate the color standards and a black metal 
diaphragm with a circular aperture 12 mm in diameter 
in the optical field. 


4.1.4 Tube Assembly 


Mount the tubes securely in a vertical and central 
position with respect to the optical viewer. Cover the 
upper ends of the tubes with removable diaphragmed 
metal caps about 25 mm in length. The caps shall be 
of sufficient diameter to slip easily over the ends of the 
tubes. The aperture in the diaphragm of the cap shall be 
14 mm in diameter. 


4.1.5 Optical Viewer 


Provide the chromometer with a suitable optical viewer 
head consisting of prisms and an eyepiece containing 
a lens. Provide prisms of a suitable form, matched in 
their refracting angles and areas, and so mounted as to 


IS 1448 [P : 14] : 2019 


Fic. 1 SAYBOLT CHROMOMETER WITH ARTIFICIAL DAYLIGHT LAMP 


avoid the possibility of disarrangement. Arrange the 
prisms so that the light rays passing through the tubes 
are deflected into an optical head and may be viewed 
by the eyepiece. The arrangement shall be such as to 
provide a circular field of vision free from distortion and 
parallax (see Note), one-half of which is illuminated by 
the light transmitted by the sample, and the other half 
by the color standard. 
NOTE — An adapter (see Fig. 3) may be used to locate the 
light rays passing up through the centre of the eyepiece. The 
adapter consists of a metal collar of such diameter as to fit the 
outside diameter of the eyepiece closely. It is approximately 
50 mm long and closed at one end with a metal diaphragm having 
a centrally located aperture approximately 2.5 mm in diameter. 


4.1.6 Illumination 


Arrange for the light to be transmitted through the 
tube by means of a reflecting mirror of either white 
opal glass or clear glass. With a uniform coating of 
untarnished silver on one surface. Fix the mirror at a 
suitable angle, and so arrange it that reflected light of 
equal intensity of radiation will pass through the tubes 


in parallel rays. Alternatively, diffused light may be 
projected directly up through the tubes from the base 
of the instrument. 


4.1.7 Light Source 


For the light source, use an artificial daylight lamp 
so arranged as to project a diffused light up through 
the tubes. The diffused light shall be free of glare or 
shadows. Interfering light from all other sources shall 
be excluded. 


4.1.8 Colour Standards 


The whole color standard and the half color standard 
shall be of such colorimetric characteristics that the 
trilinear co-ordinates x, y and z, and the luminous 
transmission TW, when calculated from the spectral 
transmission data using the 1931 ICI (International 
Commission on Illumination) Standard Illumination C, 
are as shown in Table 1. It is convenient, but not 
necessary, to mount the glasses in a turret within the 
collar mounted on the plain tube.

Table 1 Characteristics of Colour Standards 
( Clause 4.1.8 )

Limits with 


Whole Color Standard One Half Color Standard

4.1.9 Lamp 


Use a lamp bulb rated at 60 W. It shall be constructed 
of clear glass, inside frost finish, and shall be rated at 
approximately 13 lumens per watt and 2750 Kelvin 
colour temperature. Attach to a standard socket 
reflector, hemispherical in form (see Fig. 1), the interior 
surface of which is finished with a brilliant aluminum 
bronze powder, free form mica and other adulterants, 
and applied with a heat-resistant bronzing liquid 
sprayed uniformly over the surface. This finish shall be 
such as to be free from selective absorption, and have 
an initial reflectivity above 65 percent. 


4.1.10 Daylight Filter Glass (See Note) 


Concave-convex in form, and dust-tight. It shall fit 
closely over the opening in the hemispherical reflector 
(see Fig. 1). The glass filter shall be finished on its 
concave surface by sand-blasting and acid-smoothening 
or fortifying. An acceptable daylight filter shall possess 
such characteristics that the tri linear co-ordinates 
(x, y and z) and the luminous transmission TW, when 
calculated from the spectral transmission data using 
the 1931 ICI Standard Illuminant A, are as shown in 
Table 2. 


NOTE — A spectrophotometric test of an acceptable filter 
should indicate a transmission of radiant energy not less than 60 
percent at 410 nm, with a smooth curve down to a transmission 
below 10 percent at 700 nm. This curve, furthermore, should 
not have the pronounced hump that is characteristic of excess 
cobalt. The typical cobalt curve has an increased transmission 
at a wavelength of 570 nm above a straight line drawn between 
the point 540 and 590 nm, and also a transmission band in the 
red for wavelengths of 600 nm and greater. This variation in 
an acceptable filter shall not, at 570 nm, exceed 0.03 above 
the straight line drawn between 540 and 590 nm, nor shall the 
transmission for wavelength 700 nm exceed the transmission 
for any shorter wavelength, such as 600 nm, by more than 0.03. 


Table 2 Characteristics of Daylight Filter 
( Clause 4.1.10 ) 


Color Characteristic Limits 
TW 0.107 to 0.160 
X 0.314 to 0.330 
0.337 to 0.341 
Z 0.329 to 0.349 


S STANDARDIZATION OF APPARATUS 


Remove the glass from the bottom of the oil sample 
tube. Clean the disc, oil sample tube and plain tube. 
When deposits are not removable by wiping or solvent 
rinsing, wash with soap and water. After cleaning, rinse 
with distilled water and with acetone or some other 
suitable solvent, and dry. Assemble the oil sample 
tube, and position the tubes in the instrument. Using 
the specified light source and illumination, observe 
the comparative light intensity of the two-halves of 
the optical field, with both tubes empty, and with the 
12 mm diaphragm removed from under the plain 
tube. The intensity of light observed in each half of 
the optical field shall be the same. Adjustment in the 
position of the light source may be necessary to achieve 
this match. Replace the 12 mm diaphragm under the 
plain tube, and fill the oil sample tube to the sample 
tube division 20 with distilled water. The intensity of 
the light observed in each half of the optical field shall 
be the same, for the instrument to be judged satisfactory 
for use. 


6 PREPARATION OF SAMPLE 


6.1 If the material is turbid, filter through a sufficient 
number of qualitative filter paper (Whatman No. 4 or 
equivalent) until it 1s clear. 


6.2 When preparing paraffin wax for testing, do not 
heat excessively, because oxidation may occur with 
consequent discoloration of the sample. 


6.3 If the sample is contained in a clear, transparent 
container such as glass bottle, visually inspect the sample 
for evidence of free water, particulate contamination 
and haze by holding the container up to the light. If 
the sample is contained in a non-transparent container 
shake or agitate the container vigorously to uniformly 
suspend any free water that may in the sample before 
transferring a portion to a clear, transparent container to 
conduct visual inspection before proceeding. 


7 PROCEDURE FOR REFINED LIGHT OILS 
AND PHARMACEUTICAL WHITE OILS 


7.1 Flush the oil sample tube with a portion of 
the sample, taking care to allow the tube to drain 


thoroughly. Fill the oil tube with the material 
(see 7.1.1) and compare with a whole color standard. If 
the material is lighter than the color standard, remove 
the standard and replace it with a half standard. If the 
sample is darker than the single whole standard at 
sample tube division 6.25, add another whole standard. 
It is important that all materials in the color tube be free 
from air bubbles. 


7.2 With the proper color standard or standards in 
place, and the material in the oil sample tube at a level 
where its color is decidedly darker than that of the 
color standard, draw off the sample slowly by means 
of the petcock until the oil appears just slightly darker 
than the color standard. From this point, draw the 
sample level down to the nearest depth corresponding 
to color number as shown in Table 3. If the color of 
the oil observed through the eyepiece is still darker 
than the color standard, draw the oil down to the next 
depth given in Table 3, and compare. Continue this 


IS 1448 [P : 14] : 2019 


operation until a depth is reached where the sample and 
color standard match or show questionable differences 
(see 7.2.1). At this point, lower the oil column to the 
next specified depth and, if oil is unmistakably lighter 
than the color standard, record the corresponding to the 
next higher level as the Saybolt color. 


7.2.1 Experience in the use of this instrument will 
obviate the necessity of following the step-by-step 
procedure outlined in 7.2 for choosing the proper color 
standards for each sample. Examples of the procedure 
are given in Table 4. 


8 PROCEDURE FOR PETROLEUM WAX 


Heat the wax sample to 8.5 to 17?C. above its melting 
point. Preheat the oil sample tube. Pour the liquid wax 
into the oil sample tube; turn the heating elements off, 
and after the heat waves in the sample are no longer 
noticeable, obtain the required readings as directed in 7.

9 REPORTING 10 PRECISION 
Report the recorded Color units as Saybolt colour and, — Results of duplicate tests shall not differ by more than 
if the sample was filtered, add the words. the following amounts: 
Repeatability Reproducibility 
1 colour unit 2 colour units

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
